text:
Blake Lizotte hasn't scored in 22 games this season, and he's not the kind of player who was going to fill the net. What makes the drought notable is that the chances have been there: 3.1 expected goals and nothing to show for it. Our numbers call him due, and goals tend to follow chances.

He's a 13-minute center for Pittsburgh, undrafted out of St. Cloud State, who earned his way through Los Angeles. The on-ice picture is decent: the Penguins take about 54% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, a little better than without him, on a team that has won two of his last ten games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 84th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists, so the five assists aren't a fluke. NHL Edge has his acceleration in the 89th percentile.

What to watch: one goal changes the mood of a drought like this. He has 26 shots, and something should go in.
